0.0.n: Introduces a contrast with the previously discussed group.

0.2.n: Refers here to people of foreign nationality living in Japan.

0.3.n: Marks foreign residents as the topic of this statistic.

0.4.n: 約 applies to the whole increase, while 35 combines with 万 to make 350,000.

0.5.n: Japanese groups large numbers in units of 10,000; 35万 is 350,000.

0.6.n: Combines with 千 to add 4,000 to the preceding 350,000.

0.7.n: 千 means 1,000, 人 counts people, and 増 indicates an increase; 4千人増 adds 4,000 to the increase.

0.8.n: Links the amount of increase to the resulting total in this compact news expression.

0.9.n: 367万 supplies 3,670,000, followed by 7,463; 人 counts people.

1.0.n: 全 means all, and 都道府県 collectively names Japan’s four types of prefectural divisions.

1.2.n: 増加し is the linking form of 増加する, connecting this statement to what follows.

2.0.n: Names the data collection that began in 2013.

2.1.n: Marks 調査 as what was started.

2.2.n: Past form of 始める; directly describes 2013年 as the year when the surveys began.

2.3.n: 年 marks a calendar year, here modified by 調査を始めた.

2.4.n: Sets 2013 as the starting point of the period being compared, including that year.

2.5.n: Indicates the greatest count within the stated period.

2.6.n: Marks the resulting status with なる; となる sounds more formal than になる.

2.7.n: Past form of なる, showing that the number reached a new status.

3.0.n: Describes the coronavirus as a new type, forming part of the established name for the COVID-19 virus.

3.1.n: Together with 新型, refers to the virus responsible for COVID-19.

3.2.n: Marks the cause of the population decline here.

3.3.n: Combines with に to describe how long the decline lasted.

3.4.n: Turns 一時的 into a description of the decline: it lasted only a limited time.

3.5.n: 減少した is the plain past form of 減少する, reporting a completed decline.

3.6.n: Connects the earlier decline to the contrasting recent increase.

4.0.n: 年 identifies the calendar year that starts the stated run of increases.

4.2.n: Expresses a duration here, rather than a calendar year.

4.3.n: Shows that the annual increases occurred without a break.

4.4.n: Completes 3年連続で, describing the increase as occurring three years in a row.

4.5.n: 増加する in the ている form describes a continuing trend across the stated years.

0.lit: On the other hand, foreign residents: an approximately 354,000-person increase, to 3,677,463 people.
0.tip: News reports often omit the final verb when presenting statistics.

1.tip: The linking form 増加し carries the sentence forward without ending the statement.

2.lit: Since 2013, when surveys began, became the highest number.
2.tip: 調査を始めた directly modifies 2013年: the year when the surveys began.

3.lit: Due to the novel coronavirus, temporarily decreased, but
3.tip: によって identifies the cause here, while が introduces the contrast that follows.

4.lit: Since 2023, for three consecutive years, has been increasing.
4.tip: ている describes the continuing trend, not necessarily an increase happening at this exact moment.
